In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of antisense oligodeoxynucleotides (ODN) as a therapeutic tool.
the synthesis of novel nucleotide analogues and their application in the design of antisense and antigen oligonucleotide probes.
the development of novel nucleotide analogs for use as building blocks in oligonucleotide chemistry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3'-thionoformacetal (TFMA) linker is not suitable for incorporation into antisense oligonuclearotides.
the conformational flexibility of the backbone is not the only factor that influences the duplex stability, but that it is a very important factor.

the conformational preferences of the backbone modifications are different in the context of a DNA.DNA duplex and an RNA.DNA hybrid and that these differences correlate with the stability of the duplexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conformation of the backbone modification is an important factor in designing antisense oligonucloetides.
FMA linkages are preferred for the design of antisense RNA.DA hybrid duplexes and 3'-F or 3'-O-TFMA linkages are suitable for antisense DNA.DA duplexes.
the conformation of the modified nucleotides in the duplex is not necessarily a good predictor of their effect on the stability of the duplex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3'-thiopropylene linkages can be incorporated into antisense oligonucletides and that the 3'-thiolactone linkage is not required for antisense activity.
the conformation of the modified nucleotide is an important factor in determining the stability of an antisense duplex.
the 3'-thionucleoside is a more stable and better performing backbone analog than the corresponding 3'-FNA.
